decisions.difference: A: (active_condition Fever) only, plus a separate probable-Fever rule from temperature ≥ 38  vs  B: (or (active_condition Fever) (>= (measurement (snomed_concept "Body temperature" "observable entity") °C) 38)) in every trigger and fever term
decisions.reason: The page defines fever directly as 'a temperature ≥ 38°C now or in the past 3 days'; B uses that definition as the fever condition, without diagnosing a finding (Fever) as a probable diagnosis.

decisions.difference: A: (diagnosis Fever probable) from temperature ≥ 38  vs  B: no such rule
decisions.reason: Not needed once the page's temperature definition is part of each fever condition; the page names no 'fever likely' diagnosis.

decisions.difference: A: fever term (active_condition Fever)  vs  B: fever term also accepts (>= (measurement (snomed_concept "Body temperature" "observable entity") °C) 38)
decisions.reason: Same reason as the trigger: 'temperature ≥ 38°C' is the page's definition of the fever in 'patient with a fever and any of'.

decisions.difference: A: Seizure or Post-ictal state  vs  B: Seizure only
decisions.reason: The page says 'Having/just had a seizure'; a recorded Seizure covers both, and 'post-ictal' is not the page's word, so the narrower addition was not made.

decisions.difference: A: Eruption of skin (disorder)  vs  B: Eruption (morphologic abnormality) for 'rash'
decisions.reason: Both mean 'rash'; Eruption is the form VHA's vocabulary already uses (3 rules), so the same idea is written the same way.

decisions.difference: A: Skin lesion (disorder)  vs  B: Lesion + finding_site Skin structure
decisions.reason: 'lesion/s of skin' has an exact precoordinated concept; prefer it to a postcoordinated morphology.

decisions.difference: A: Lesion of genitalia  vs  B: Lesion + finding_site Genital structure
decisions.reason: 'lesion/s of ... genitals' has an exact precoordinated concept.

decisions.difference: A: Lesion of rectum  vs  B: Lesion + finding_site Rectum structure
decisions.reason: 'lesion/s of ... rectum' has an exact precoordinated concept.

decisions.difference: A: Oral lesion  vs  B: Lesion + finding_site Oral cavity structure
decisions.reason: 'lesion/s of ... mouth' has an exact precoordinated concept.

decisions.difference: A: Lesion of eye  vs  B: Lesion + finding_site Structure of eye proper
decisions.reason: 'lesion/s of ... eyes' has an exact precoordinated concept.

decisions.difference: A: Pseudomembrane + finding_site Nasal cavity structure  vs  B: Pseudomembrane + finding_site Nasal structure
decisions.reason: The page says 'in nose/throat'; Nasal structure (the nose) is the page's word, not only the cavity.

decisions.difference: A: Common cold  vs  B: Common cold + qualifier Recent
A: tick present = Infestation caused by Ixodidae  vs  B: Ixodidae or Argasidae (also in the viral rule's 'no' list)
decisions.reason: The page says 'tick present' without restricting to hard ticks; both tick families are ticks.

decisions.difference: A: no check_for of Headache, Backache, Fatigue, Sore throat, Cough  vs  B: checks for them
decisions.final_expr: Headache, Backache, Fatigue, Sore throat, Cough (clinical_finding)
decisions.reason: These are the page's mpox, diphtheria and acute-viral-infection criteria ('headache/backache/body pain', 'fatigue, sore throat/nasal congestion/cough', 'sore throat'), so they belong in the approach task's check_for.

decisions.difference: A: Spotted fever group rickettsial disease  vs  B: South African tick-bite fever
decisions.reason: The page says 'Tick bite fever'; 'South African tick-bite fever' is the SNOMED name closest to those words, but the page does not say which rickettsia (African tick bite fever is the other child of A's parent concept).

decisions.difference: A: '… in fever' / 'Urgent: fever with danger signs'  vs  B: '… from fever page' / 'Urgent: fever with red-box danger signs'
decisions.reason: B's names are more specific to this page, which reduces the chance of colliding with another page's description.

notes: Both builds passed. Base B (its fever condition follows the page's ≥ 38°C definition and its approach task checks for every mpox/diphtheria/viral criterion). From A: the precoordinated lesion concepts for skin, genitals, rectum, mouth and eyes (anus stays Lesion + Anal structure in both). A's 'probable Fever' rule and Post-ictal state were not carried over. Two decisions are unsettled (Post-ictal state; the tick bite fever concept) and are in Questions for a clinician. Neither build encodes malaria (no SNOMED concept for 'been in a malaria area') or the 'none of the above' precondition on the tick/viral rules; both are recorded under Could not model / SNOMED gaps.
